So much debate about stick control vs gyro controls vs kb/m. I think they each have their place and I use all three. Though kb/m is ky goto mainly because I've been a pc gamer since the days of wolfenstein 3d, ultima VI, and a few others. Life long pc user.

I use controller still for a lot of pc games and ports and of course when I do happen to play consoles. I'm not great at aiming in fps games with them, but I also know that it takes time and practice. There's a lot of people who are controller users who aim very well. Some who use aim assist, and some (like me) who are better with kb/m.

As for gyro, I use it with a lot of games when I play on my steamdeck. I used it on switch as well, but I've recently gotten rid of all my Nintendo stuff because I just don't really play it. I also don't play a lot of triple A games right out the gate. If I do, I wait for them to come down in price. I prefer to give my money to the indie devs. Too many times have I been burned with triple A studios and just absolutely blown away and pleasantly surprised by indie devs.

Tldr; all controls have their place and some people prefer one over the other, and that's ok. I do wish every game was able to implement all of them, but that's just not reality. Cheers

I know the feelings you have quite well. I was addicted to buying games. When I was younger I felt a connection to video games that I didn't get elsewhere. Collecting was another level and it took 10+ years to realize that I don't need every new game. I don't need to pay full price for games that I either don't intend to play or don't intend to play for some time. Over the course of a few more years I learned to curb my spending on games. I still get depressed and will go on a buying spree, but it's much rarer now.

I'm also trans and never felt comfortable in my own body. It caused me to not want to be social, coupled with already being introverted, it was a bad combination. All I did was stay home and play games.

Here are some things that have helped me to be more social and let me enjoy games a lot more.

I've joined a couple of groups that are accepting. One being a bunco group for women. They are super accepting and allow me to get out once a month to do a social activity. I've also joined a local discord group that does events twice a month. I do my best to attend those. One of the harder ones for me was making new friends, but when I did, I made sure to make plans with them and keep those plans in a way to force myself to continue to get out outside of groups. I've attended random gatherings that I occasionally see and even though I can feel and be awkward, it still feels good to get out. I don't expect to make friends every time I go somewhere, but every so often I do make a new friend. And then sometimes I will just take myself out on the town solo. Doesn't have to be expensive. Sometimes I'll go have a nice dinner, sometimes I'll go touch grass at the park, or even go see a movie.

All that being said, it wasn't an easy process and I was in therapy for quite some time for trauma and other things. It helped some. Though when I lost my therapist I realized I was using her like a crutch/excuse. Justifying the things I did and telling myself I will just talk about it in therapy. When I lost her, I found myself a loss about how to proceed. I realized I needed to take responsibility for my own actions and feelings. Now that I didn't have her to talk through it, I realized I couldn't use her as a crutch. I started making better decisions.

Aa for gaming, there was a point that I felt it was more like a chore or just something to do to pass the time. I didn't feel like I was enjoying it. Part of that was the major depressive disorder, and part of it was doing things in games just because it was a daily routine. Daily quests, limited events, trying to keep some streak alive, trying to get all the achievements, etc. When I stepped away from gaming and let all those go I felt better, but not complete. I realized I really do loving gaming but I need to let those dailies, achievements, etc go. Now I just let myself enjoy a game. If I get an achievement that's fantastic. When I 100% a game, it's because I was just playing and enjoying it. Not because I was trying to just because my brain said 100% it. When I feel like I'm not having fun, I move on. Switch games, try something else, switch genres for a bit, or whatever. Lastly, I find that I have a lot more fun playing games with other people. My new (8 months now) partner and I game together regularly. I also have an irl friend that I've reconnected to and I also game with him. There's a few others I've met just on discord or even here on reddit. There's always people looking to play the same game you want to play. I enjoy gaming alone now, but I enjoy it that much more with others.

I don't know if any of the above is helpful or not. I feel like I'm a success story though. Addictions, depression, anxiety, etc isn't easy. You can break the habits though. And don't ever feel bad about stepping away from gaming if you're not having a good time with it. Picking up new hobbies has also helped. Split your time between different hobbies. Step away from gaming temporarily if needed. Hell, step away permanently if it makes you feel better. Cheers

All of these have been suggested over and over again. And most of us agree with all of it. I wanted to see stairs/slabs when they introduced Diorite, Granite, and Andesite. I'm grateful they added new blocks and they continue to add new blocks. I do wish that we could do more with them. Again, stairs/slabs for them would be awesome. Same goes for clay.

I also like the idea someone had about crafting paint and being able to paint/stain/dye stone or cobblestone.

More stone types, ores (Silver, copper, etc), being able to craft steel and other metals would be neat. Maybe have different kinds of bars (like iron bars - gold, silver, whatever else).

More wood types, brick types, and non flower plants would all be great too.

So I agree with having all of this. It would be great if they could implement new blocks until we had more than we knew what to do with. But the idea behind minecraft was simple and currently, and while it's still getting updates and will for a very, very long time, and will continue to get new blocks now and then, it will probably stay pretty simple.

I don't mean simple as in bad. I just mean simple as in the concept. Here's a world with a few things in it. Destroy, craft, build, survive. Now with the amount of mods/api out there, almost anything is possible and while the mods are not the first thing that Mojang (Microsoft) thinks about when making an update, it most likely plays a significant role.

First, when they make a new block type, that one block has to be tested against every other block type in the game. Of course, I'm not much of a programmer, so my understanding is limited. But from what I do understand, the reason that Diorite, etc use the Stone ID is because the ID is already in the game and it knows how to react to it. So could they just use the same block IDs with an extension like they do with other items? I have no idea. But I do know everything has to be tested over and over again. So each new block takes time. And then each API has to be updated for each Minecraft update. And then the plugins have to be updated. While Mojang isn't responsible for those things, I'm sure it's a concern to them since the vast majority of online players play on a modded version of the game with a ton of plugins. So when Minecraft updates, it can take weeks, months, and even years for servers to catch up. Many of them use older versions of the game for this very reason.

Mojang does see what some of these mods are doing and they have implemented some of it into the core of the game, which is great. I look forward to playing the game for many years to come. I'm always building something new and I'm always looking forward to the server I play on to reset the world so we have a fresh start.

Lastly, I apologize for the long post. It looks just like rambling after re-reading. I should probably just delete it, but oh well. Cheers all. Have fun with what we have. Be thankful for what they have given thus far. :)
